sections.h2: How do I sell a Pittsford house on a short timeline?
sections.html:
Pittsford owners can use a broker, sell privately or accept a cash offer, and the town's rules on permits, septic and village boundaries are worth checking before you pick. Pittsford is a suburb about seven miles southeast of Rochester, with homes concentrated around Pittsford village and a long list of Erie Canal landmarks.

Cash is attractive when a house needs updates that a mortgage lender would flag, when an estate has to settle, or when a move has a fixed date. With a median home value near $389,100, even a modest discount for a quick as-is sale adds up in dollars, so compare offers carefully.

Pittsford covers 23.41 square miles in the southeast of Monroe County. Mendon lies to its south, Perinton to the east, Henrietta and Brighton to the west and Brighton and Penfield to the north. The village of Pittsford was incorporated in 1827, and the Erie Canal's completion in 1825 brought mills and commerce, followed by the Auburn and Rochester Railroad in 1840. Old canal buildings along Schoen Place now hold restaurants and shops.

In 1996 the town adopted its Greenprint plan, buying development rights on roughly two-thirds of its remaining farmland, and it was the first town in New York to preserve open space that way. Eleven town parks, the Lock 32 double lock and the Erie Canal trail give the town a lot of public space, and Powder Mills and Mendon Ponds county parks lie inside its borders.

The Pittsford Central School District runs two high schools, Sutherland and Mendon, plus the Barker Road and Calkins Road middle schools. Its five elementary schools are Jefferson, Park, Thornell, Mendon Center and Allen Creek. Allendale Columbia School, an independent school for nursery through grade 12, and St. Louis School are also in town, and two colleges, St. John Fisher and Nazareth, are located in Pittsford.

School reputation is a main selling point here, and buyers sometimes ask for the attendance zone of a particular address. Ask the district office to confirm the school assignment before you quote it in a listing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Pittsford housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 30,617 residents in 2020 and estimates 30,588 for July 1, 2025. For 2020 to 2024 it reports:

  • Owner-occupied rate: 86.4 percent, so very few homes are rented.
  • Median owner-occupied value: $389,100.
  • Median household income: $145,581, across 10,528 households.
  • Median gross rent: $1,534.
  • Residents with a bachelor's degree or higher: 74.6 percent.
  • Mean commute: 19.0 minutes.

With so few rentals, nearly every sale involves a homeowner who has built up equity and a buyer who is moving into the district. Investor-owned houses are a small niche.

sections.h2: How and when are Pittsford property taxes paid?
sections.html:
The Town Clerk and Tax Office collects both bills. School tax is due in full on October 1, and the clerk's page lists later deadlines in the table below.

Pittsford tax payment schedule from the Town Clerk and Tax Office
BillDeadlineDetail
School taxOctober 1Full payment at Town Hall with 2 percent interest through October 31.
School tax, lateNovember 1 through 18Monroe County Treasury only, with 5 percent interest. Nothing is accepted after November 18.
Town and county taxFebruary 10Interest of 1.5 percent a month after that date.
Town and county installmentsFebruary 28, March 31, April 30Second, third and fourth installments.
Town and county tax, after May 31Monroe County TreasurerCall (585) 753-1200 for the amount due.

School installments run October 15 and November 15, paid to the County Treasurer. Unpaid school balances roll onto the next year's town and county bill.

sections.h2: What does the assessor's calendar look like in Pittsford?
sections.html:
Pittsford assesses at full value and follows the state calendar. The valuation date is July 1 of the previous year, and the taxable status date is March 1, when all exemption forms must be on file. Informal reviews run from July 1 to March 1, any change is mailed between May 1 and May 15, and the formal review falls on the fourth Tuesday in May, which will be May 25, 2027.

Exemptions the Assessor's Office lists include:

  • Basic STAR, with an income cap of $500,000, and Enhanced STAR at $110,750 for the 2026 roll.
  • Senior Citizens with Limited Income, capped at $58,400 for town and county and $37,400 for school.
  • Disability with Limited Income, with the same caps.
  • Alternative and Cold War Veterans.
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, worth 10 percent of assessed value.

New STAR applicants register with the State and receive a credit check instead of an exemption on the school bill. The assessor can be reached at (585) 248-6230.

sections.h2: What do Pittsford's code and zoning rules cover?
sections.html:
Pittsford requires building permits for construction, additions, alterations and demolition, pools, signs, sheds, decks, basement finishing and generators. After a permit is issued and the work meets zoning, a certificate of occupancy is issued. The Design Review and Historic Preservation Board reviews architectural plans for new structures and renovations, and the Zoning Board of Appeals hears variance requests.

Other points matter to sellers. Sewer service reaches about 70 percent of the town, so the rest use septic systems. Fences are capped at 3 feet in front of the front setback line and 6 feet behind it. Junk vehicles are prohibited, and garbage is collected by private haulers that owners hire. Parking on public highways is banned from November 15 to April 1. Code Enforcement can be reached at (585) 248-6265.

sections.h2: What should a Pittsford seller prepare before listing?
sections.html:
Pittsford buyers tend to ask detailed questions, so having answers ready helps a sale move. Consider gathering these items:

  • The deed and any lot survey, along with permits for pools, decks and finished basements.
  • Whether the house is on public sewer or a septic system.
  • Recent school and town and county tax bills, plus any exemption you currently hold.
  • The name of your private garbage hauler and any refuse district fees.

The Assessor's Property Sales Report and the Monroe County property portal give comparable sale prices for pricing the house.

sections.h2: How do I know if my Pittsford house is in the village?
sections.html:
The village of Pittsford sits in the middle of the town along routes 96 and 31, and it was incorporated separately in 1827. A house inside it may carry village charges on top of town ones, so confirm the location of your parcel. The Monroe County Real Property Portal shows tax parcel records, and the Pittsford Assessor's Office can confirm specific parcels.

County delinquent-tax foreclosure also reaches here. Monroe County's Action No. 150 covers parcels in Pittsford, including the village, and set a public auction for September 11, 2026, which has passed. Anyone behind on taxes should call the County Treasury before the next list is filed.

faqs.q: How much is a typical house worth in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median value of $389,100 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024 data. Individual houses vary with school zone, lot size and condition, so use recent comparable sales.

faqs.q: When are Pittsford school taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with full payment accepted at Town Hall through October 31 with 2 percent interest. From November 1 through 18 only the Monroe County Treasury takes payment, with 5 percent interest, and nothing is accepted after November 18.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May. The 2026 date was May 26, and the next is May 25, 2027. The Assessment Review Board has five members and meets once a year.
About 70 percent of the town is on community sewer service. Properties outside those areas use private septic systems, which a buyer will likely want inspected.

faqs.q: Who can I call about a permit in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The Code Enforcement and Building Department at Town Hall, 11 South Main Street, at (585) 248-6265. It issues permits and the certificates of occupancy and compliance.
